platform/lib/completion_predicate.py:559 calls bare jsonschema.validate, which raises Unresolvable on the https://ast-integrate.invalid/ $ref carried by all 230 command-center/schema/ class shims (8/8 sampled). evaluate() turns that into condition 4 NOT-CHECKED, hence INDETERMINATE, so the sound reader can never return COMPLETE for a real catalogued unit -- and its rejection of a truncated artifact therefore carries no truncation information. The repo's own platform/lib/schema_resolver.py:build_registry() resolves the same shim.

completion_predicate._c4 validates a .jsonl artifact with a single json.loads(whole file), so any multi-line JSONL is UNSATISFIED at 100% ('Extra data: line 2 column 1'). The rejection curve is flat, so the reader cannot distinguish a truncated JSONL from an intact one.

76 of 78 work-unit-artifact-writing modules, including the canonical producer command-center/p13_emit_receipt.py:727 (OUT.write_text(...)), write the artifact non-atomically to its final path with no tmp+os.replace. That is the mechanism that puts a truncated artifact at the real path in the first place; D1/D2 are what then accept it.

q2_is_there_a_schema_where_a_truncated_a.answer: YES, in two distinct mechanisms, both executed.
q2_is_there_a_schema_where_a_truncated_a.mechanism_1_sentinel_inside_the_artifact: For any artifact class whose reader does not gate on a full parse, the sentinel is a substring search over whatever bytes survive. Measured on markdown-sentinel-mid (3,459 B synthetic) and on the real TST-0334/TST-0350 receipts: the legacy reader accepts a 16% file because the sentinel, written early, is still present.
q2_is_there_a_schema_where_a_truncated_a.mechanism_2_sentinel_outside_the_artifac: receipt_schema_gate checks the sentinel carried by the RECEIPT, which is written independently of the payload. The payload is never opened at all, so the sentinel is 'before the payload' in the strongest sense and a 2%-truncated artifact passes.
